issues.title: Improve README.md for new contributors and developers
issues.body:
The current README.md provides an overview of AnkiDroid and links to several resources, but it can be difficult for new contributors to quickly understand the repository structure and find the appropriate documentation. Since AnkiDroid has a comprehensive wiki, user manual, and contribution guides spread across multiple locations, first-time contributors may spend significant time navigating between resources.

The project documentation already encourages contributions from both developers and non-developers, and improving onboarding documentation could make the contribution process smoother.

Proposed improvements

I would like to improve the README.md by adding or reorganizing sections such as:

A clearer "Getting Started" section for contributors.
A high-level overview of the repository structure and important modules.
A dedicated "Documentation" section linking to:
Development Guide
Contribution Guide
User Manual
Issue tracker
A contributor onboarding checklist.
Links to beginner-friendly issues such as good first issue and help wanted.
A short explanation of the technologies used (Kotlin, Gradle, Android tooling, etc.).

Benefits

These changes would:

Reduce the onboarding time for new contributors.
Make important resources easier to discover.
Encourage more community contributions.
Improve the overall developer experience.

I would be happy to work on this improvement and submit a pull request if the maintainers think this would be useful.

issues.title: [BUG] Locale-only {{tts}} selects an unavailable voice instead of an installed voice
issues.body:
### Checked for duplicates?

- [x] This issue is not a duplicate

### Does it also happen in the desktop version?

- [x] This bug does not occur in the latest version of Anki Desktop (26.05)

### What are the steps to reproduce this bug?

1. Use Google as Android's preferred TTS engine, with an installed French voice.
2. Use a locale-only native TTS tag in a card template:

   ```html
   {{tts fr_FR:Front}}
   ```

3. Review the card.

AnkiDroid reports:

```text
ERROR_NOT_INSTALLED_YET
```

The same failure occurs with `es_ES`, despite installed French and Spanish voices that work in Android's TTS settings.

As a control, pinning an exact installed voice works:

```html
{{tts fr_FR voices=EXACT_INSTALLED_VOICE:Front}}
```

### Expected behaviour

When no voice is explicitly requested, locale-only selection should prefer a matching voice where `unavailable() == false`, and TTS should play normally.

### Actual behaviour

Locale-only selection takes the first matching voice regardless of availability, so it can select a voice marked `KEY_FEATURE_NOT_INSTALLED` and fail with `ERROR_NOT_INSTALLED_YET`.

AnkiDroid detects unavailable voices here:

https://github.com/ankidroid/Anki-Android/blob/ebcf8e0e34921628b9b8a496c66ffd4adbb3705f/AnkiDroid/src/main/java/com/ichi2/anki/TtsVoices.kt#L261-L265

Upstream moved the note editor's control from Python to TypeScript and now serves it as a backend web page ([ankitects/anki#4029](https://github.com/ankitects/anki/issues/4029), tracking [ankitects/anki#3830](https://github.com/ankitects/anki/issues/3830)) the same mechanism we already use for deck options, graphs, card-info, etc. This proposes bringing that editor into AnkiDroid behind a developer-options flag, reusing the existing AnkiServer stack.

## High-level steps (in order)
- Backend bump: In Anki-Android-Backend, move the anki submodule past [#4029](https://github.com/ankitects/anki/issues/4029)
-  Consume the new backend in AnkiDroid
- Add the experimental flag and create the editor fragment

issues.title: Feature Proposal: Semantic Duplicate Detection for Cards
issues.body:
### Problem

Users may unintentionally create multiple cards that are phrased differently but contain essentially the same information. Over time, these semantic duplicates can increase deck size unnecessarily and add extra review workload.

Examples:

* "What is TCP?"
* "Define TCP."
* "What does TCP stand for and what is its purpose?"

Although these cards are not exact duplicates, they represent very similar knowledge.

### Proposed Solution

When a user creates or edits a card, AnkiDroid could optionally analyze its semantic similarity with existing cards in the deck and warn the user if highly similar cards are found.

The goal would not be to automatically delete or merge cards, but simply to inform users about potential duplicates and allow them to decide whether to continue.

### Potential Benefits

* Reduce accidental duplicate cards.
* Keep decks cleaner and easier to maintain.
* Reduce unnecessary review workload.
* Improve study efficiency.

Before investing significant implementation effort, I would like to know whether maintainers think this feature aligns with AnkiDroid's goals and whether such a contribution would be welcome.

issues.body:
### Checked for duplicates?

- [x] This issue is not a duplicate

### Does it also happen in the desktop version?

- [x] This bug does not occur in the latest version of Anki Desktop

### What are the steps to reproduce this bug?

Hi AnkiDroid Team,

I’m a PhD student researching Android performance issues. My research group recently ran a static analysis scan for main-thread blocking bugs, and our prototype flagged a potential issue in AnkiDroid.

## Checked target

+ APK-level caller: `com.ichi2.anki.Reviewer#onCollectionLoaded(Collection) / reviewer UI initialization`
+ Detected API: `project-local @WorkerThread API: com.ichi2.anki.MetaDB#getMicToolbarState`
+ Observed context: `main/UI` thread
+ Expected context: `worker/background` thread

## What I found

The analyzer reported that the app call:

```kotlin
val isMicToolbarEnabled = MetaDB.getMicToolbarState(this, parentDid)
```

from a main/UI-thread path.

This is a project-defined `@WorkerThread` contract violation, not an Android SDK API contract violation. The concrete sink is `MetaDB`, AnkiDroid's SQLite metadata helper annotated at object level with `@WorkerThread`; the synchronous call is reached from a UI path.

## Verified bug trace

```text
com.ichi2.anki.Reviewer#onCollectionLoaded(Collection) / reviewer UI initialization
  -> source location: AnkiDroid/src/main/java/com/ichi2/anki/Reviewer.kt:393
  -> source call: val isMicToolbarEnabled = MetaDB.getMicToolbarState(this, parentDid)
  -> Reviewer.onCollectionLoaded runs during reviewer UI initialization
  -> it restores deck-specific whiteboard and microphone-toolbar state synchronously
  -> calls/reaches MetaDB, an AnkiDroid SQLite metadata helper annotated with @WorkerThread
  -> MetaDB may open or upgrade ankidroid.db before the metadata query/write returns
  -> MetaDB then performs synchronous SQLite rawQuery/update/insert work
  -> this belongs to a reviewer metadata-state cluster, not just one isolated line
  -> analyzer/source audit observed

issues.title: Incremental Jetpack Compose adoption
issues.body:
Jetpack Compose for AnkiDroid incrementally, starting with a new shared `:ui-compose` module that houses the theme bridge and reusable UI components. Existing Views/Fragments stay; new screens and migrated leaf screens render in Compose hosted inside the current Fragment shells via `ComposeView`.

> FYI: At I/O 2026 Google formally moved Android UI to "Compose First":
> 
> - Android Views, Fragments, RecyclerView, ViewPager, and `android.widget` are in **maintenance mode** critical bug fixes only, no new features ([source](https://android-developers.googleblog.com/2026/05/android-ui-development-is-compose-first.html)).
> - All new Android Studio UI tooling targets Compose (Layout Editor / Navigation Editor are frozen).
> - Compose BOM 2026.04.01 (Compose 1.11) ships Grid, FlexBox, Style API, faster SlotTable runtime ([release notes](https://android-developers.googleblog.com/2026/04/jetpack-compose-april-2026-updates.html)).
> - The official guidance is interop-first incremental adoption via `AndroidView` / `ComposeView` ([interop docs](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/migrate/interoperability-apis)).
> 
> What its worth, AnkiDroid is well-positioned: AGP 9, Kotlin 2.3, minSdk 24, no Hilt/Dagger lock-in, view binding already enabled, small custom-View footprint.

## Proposed approach

### Phase 0 Foundations 
- [ ] Enable Compose in `:AnkiDroid` build (compose BOM, kotlin-compose plugin, `buildFeatures.compose = true`)
- [ ] Create `:ui-compose` module (theme + shared components)
- [ ] Document conventions in `docs/development/compose.md`

### Phase 1:  Pilot leaf screens (separate PRs, one per screen)
Low-risk, no shared state, prove the patterns:
- `AboutFragment` (static content)
- `LoadingDialogFragment`, `AsyncDialogFragment` (dialogs)
- `PageFragment` (WebView + toolbar- proves `AndroidView` interop) ,etc

### Phase 2: Mid-complexity
- Settings sub-screens (will need a strategy for custom `Preference` subclasses)
- Info / help screens

issues.body:
### Description:
Currently, the Card Browser displays all tags irrespective of the selected notes. This can make tag navigation cluttered and less relevant when working with a filtered subset of notes.

### Expected Behavior:
When notes are selected in the Card Browser, only the tags associated with those selected notes should be displayed in the tag list/filter section.
